correctness.rationale: Eliminating b and using the bijection u=2a−x gives 3xu²=4y−x³. For a unit x, the target is affine-equivalent to u²: the (p²−p)/2 unit squares each have two simple roots and zero has p roots. For x=pv≠0, first require y=pw, then cancel p from the congruence before reducing to 3v u²=4w modulo p; each solution has p lifts. This gives one fiber of size p and (p−1)/2 of size 2p for each of the p−1 such x. At x=0 there is only the fiber at y=0 of size p². These cases give exactly the stated histogram, including p²−1 fibers of size p. Summing nonempty fibers and squared multiplicities gives the stated support and energy. Frequency orthogonality contributes p⁴ and the coefficient normalization contributes p⁻⁸, so the constant-input moment is energy divided by p⁴ as asserted. An independent per-slice direct enumeration verified all of these multiplicity levels and energy for p=5,7,11,19,29; at p=5 the histogram in level order is (392,200,24,8,1).
residual_risks: The argument relies on units 2 and 3 and on modulus exactly p². The moment is for constant input with counting measure; it is not an operator norm or a weighted extremizer theorem.

value.rationale: The first nonreduced level is a natural comparison with the field cubic graph. The exact ordered convolution partition quantifies the singular strata that the field and the normalized moment alone do not exhibit; it yields exact support and a test value for ring extension problems. The square-root step uses standard lifting, but the motivated, complete decomposition of the graph convolution is the useful result, not the lifting fact itself.
residual_risks: No claim of a sharp weighted norm or of a new general lifting theorem.
